title: IR blaster fires but fan does not respond -- stepped diagnostic
description:
Fan stopped responding to the blaster on the night of 2026-08-17 (first bad
window 2026-08-18T03:48Z = 23:48 local, 5 presses in 40s). Watch reports
RELAYED / "relay: empty reply", which is the app's SUCCESS state, not an error.

ESTABLISHED 2026-08-18 -- do NOT retest:
- Fan is powered and works via the real remote (owner).
- Real remote works FROM THE BLASTER'S POSITION, so room geometry, line of
  sight and the fan's IR receiver are all fine (owner).
- Blaster's IR LED visibly emits (owner).
- Watch -> phone -> webhook -> automation -> button.press measured working:
  automation.bangle_ir_blaster_fan_power last_triggered 2026-08-18T13:24:05Z,
  context user_id null (webhook-originated).
- Blaster online at 192.168.0.6: ping 0% loss, TCP 6053 open, web_server 200.
  Uptime 664408s = 7.69d, so no reboot since the 2026-08-10 bedroom move.
- Blaster transmits and self-decodes as Symphony data=0xD81 nbits=12. Two
  captures ~5 min apart match in structure (24 burst pairs) within +/-2 units
  of jitter, so transmission is stable and repeatable.
- HA-side artefacts CANNOT prove actuation (validation.md R15): ESPHome buttons
  are stateless, button.* state is HA's local last_pressed, and
  automation.last_triggered only says the automation started.

DEGRADATION PATTERN (button.* history): single presses 08-11..08-14, then 4
presses on 08-15, 2 on 08-16, single on 08-17, then 5 in 40s on 08-18 03:48Z
and nothing since. Progressive decay, not a step change.

REMAINING UNKNOWNS: content (does the pattern match the real remote), amplitude
(does it carry across the room), framing (carrier / duty / command_repeats).
Carrier is NOT measurable from our captures -- the 5990 hands ESPHome a
demodulated signal, so the 006D in the pronto header is the dumper's assumption.

TOGGLE SEMANTICS: Fan Power is a toggle and the fan is currently ON, so success
in every step below is the fan CHANGING STATE, not "turning on".

FAST TRIGGER for iteration: http://192.168.0.6/ (ESPHome web UI) has both
buttons; this cuts watch/phone/Gadgetbridge/webhook/HA out of the loop.

STEP 1 -- CONTENT. Capture the real remote on the blaster's own receiver and
diff against the blaster's self-capture. Stored code was captured 2026-08-09,
BEFORE the 08-10 move to the bedroom. Differ -> flash the captured code, done.
Identical -> content eliminated, go to Step 2.

STEP 2 -- AMPLITUDE (no wiring touched). Dark room, phone camera. Compare real
remote LED vs blaster LED at the same ~6in. Check BOTH 5990 emitters (one
vertical, one horizontal). Dimmer / only one lit -> Step 3. Comparable -> Step 5.
Context: VIN is deliberately at 3V not 5V (pin-safe receiver line), and
docs/hardware.md states this "caps emitter range".

STEP 3 -- CONNECTIONS. Reseat all four 4045 leads, esp. red (VIN/3V) and green
(IRout/GPIO27). Pinch tinned tips. docs/wiring.md: "The breadboard is the least
rugged link for a permanent fixture." Fits the 3-day decay. Permanent fix is
soldering the four leads to the Feather; no firmware change.

STEP 4 -- PROXIMITY. Only if 2 and 3 inconclusive. Move blaster to within 1-2ft
of the fan's receiver, repower, fire. Works close but not at normal spot ->
range problem (reorient board to the other emitter LED, or drive a separate 5V
emitter). Fails at 1ft -> Step 5. CAVEAT: moving disturbs the breadboard, so a
fix after moving may be Step 3's reseat rather than proximity -- hence 3 first.

STEP 5 -- FRAMING. Fire the Symphony probe button (decoded form, state unknown,
never pressed since it was added 2026-08-09). If that also fails, OTA variant
buttons: command_repeats above the default 2, and carrier at 36kHz and 40kHz.

STEP 6 -- RECEIVER STATE. Only if 1-5 pass. Press blaster, then immediately try
the real remote. If the remote also stops working briefly, the blaster is
jamming/confusing the receiver rather than failing to reach it.

RULED OUT: the off-network watch press. The watch URL is a bare LAN IP
(192.168.0.70), so off-LAN it times out at the phone and never reaches HA -- no
trace, no state. Automation is mode:single with current:0 (nothing stuck), the
ESP32 never rebooted, and the watch app is stateless between taps with a 10s
watchdog. Nothing carries forward.
notes:
CARRIER PROBE RESULT 2026-08-18 -- HYPOTHESIS DISPROVED.

OTA flashed (owner ran it; 'OTA successful'). Fired 3x each, HTTP 200 on 9/9:
  38kHz (production): 3/3 received, 3/3 decoded 0xD81
  0Hz (unmodulated) : 0/3 -- NO RECEIVER EVENT AT ALL in its window
  20kHz (out of band): 3/3 received, 2/3 decoded

The 0Hz probe produced literally nothing, so the 5990's receiver DEMODULATES.
It does NOT decode via proximity overload or supply coupling. My earlier
caveat to the contrary is WRONG and is retracted. Consequence: the production
button's 42/42 clean decodes ARE real evidence that a properly modulated
carrier leaves the emitter. CARRIER LOSS IS RULED OUT.

RESIDUAL LIMIT (a limit, not a lead): 20kHz still got through, so this receiver
has a wide passband and CANNOT pin exact carrier frequency or modulation depth.
A fault where the LED emits mostly DC with only a weak 38kHz component would
still decode at 2in, still look bright on camera, and still starve the fan at
distance. Not measurable with anything on hand -- needs a scope or photodiode.

STATE: remote diagnosis is EXHAUSTED. Eliminated with measurements: code
content, amplitude, aim, delivery reliability, repeat count, runtime state
(power cycle), and carrier presence/modulation. Owner constraints (fan fine,
remote fine, position unchanged) are established and must not be retested.

NEXT AND ONLY CHEAP TEST: aim the blaster at a DIFFERENT IR device (TV,
soundbar). Capture that device's remote on the 5990, add a button, fire it.
 - cannot control it either -> emitter path at fault -> SWAP THE 5990
 - controls it fine        -> emitter proven good end-to-end; fault is specific
                              to this fan and invisible to every instrument here
Otherwise: swap the 5990 by elimination -- it is the only component in the
chain never independently tested.

CLEANUP OWED: two temporary PROBE buttons remain in ir-blaster-livingroom.yaml
and must be removed once resolved (original backed up at /tmp/irb.bak, though
/tmp is volatile -- git is the real baseline). Also .venv.broken-20260818 is
left in the repo from a venv this session damaged and should be deleted.

title: Spike: prove the UNO+WiFi R3 (ESP8266) can run the IR sniffer/blaster role
description: Owner has a UNO+WiFi R3 ATmega328P+ESP8266 CH340 (4MB flash ESP8266, external antenna) sitting around; if its ESP8266 half can run ESPHome remote_receiver/remote_transmitter, it becomes a candidate for the enclosed (Altoids tin) build where the Feather's PCB antenna dies. All ESP8266 pins are broken out on female headers (owner confirmed). Isolated on branch esp8266-uno-wifi-spike; main untouched. Test vehicle: uno-wifi-test.yaml — no wifi/api/ota/secrets, serial-only, GPIO5 RX / GPIO4 TX (only two non-strap interrupt-capable pins), and an every-15s Symphony loopback self-test using data=0x5A5 (deliberately NOT the fan's 0xD81) so it can never actuate the living-room fan. Pass = log shows the transmitted code decoded by the device's own receiver, mirroring the loopback behavior proven on the Feather 2026-08-09. ESP8266 caveat: bit-banged IR (no RMT), so this spike proves capability, not equivalence — an R1-style gate on real hardware still applies before trusting it.
notes: CORRECTION (roborev 3445, HIGH, verified in vendored source): on-device loopback is impossible on ESP8266 — remote_transmitter bit-bangs under InterruptLock (remote_transmitter.cpp:86-103) while remote_receiver captures via GPIO ISR (remote_receiver.cpp:74), so the device cannot hear its own TX. Test restructured to two legs: RX = point real fan remote at 5990, expect Received Symphony 0xD81; TX = 0x5A5 beacon every 15s, witnessed by a second receiver (Feather on ir-wiring-test.yaml or the prod living-room device's dump: all). Status: firmware flashed and booting on the HW-649 (DIP switches were hidden under factory kapton film; 5,6,7 to flash, 5,6 for logs); TX beacon confirmed firing in logs. Awaiting 5990 rewire + two-leg verification.
